problem: Metric-map-based ObjectNav methods (SemExp, PONI, ANS) need accurate global pose and heavy interactive RL training, and they cannot correct their priors when the test environment contradicts training. Prior graph-based priors (rooms only, ambiguous zones, action-based edges) do not capture place-object relations.
motivation: Real robots have noisy odometry and actuation, so methods depending on a precise metric map degrade. Humans navigate using common-sense place-object and place-place relations, which can be learned cheaply from non-interactive exploration and updated online.
key_idea: Aggregate semantic graph maps (place clusters, images, objects) from many training scenes into a Semantic Environment Atlas of place reachability and place-object probabilities, then plan semantic paths over it without a global metric map, updating relations Bayesian-style during the episode.
insight: Place-based subgoal selection matters: random subgoals give 29.2 SR, place-based subgoals 36.4, and adding the place-based stop 39.0 (Table ablation). Episodic relation updates raise SR from 33.3 to 39.0 with almost the same SPL, showing that the gain comes from replanning after a wrong place guess, at the cost of longer paths. Using semantic reachability instead of a metric map makes the agent robust to pose noise.
method: Semantic Graph Map: incrementally built graph of place, image and object nodes. Image nodes are added when cosine similarity falls below 0.8; object nodes come from MaskRCNN detections with a similarity threshold of 0.8 and matching category.

Place encoder: ResNet18 with a graph conv over up to 10 objects, taking a panoramic image, object features and object categories. It is trained with contrastive place loss, near loss and K-means cluster loss (PCL-style) into 50 place clusters.

SEA construction: place reachability Γ is the fraction of scenes where two clusters are connected among scenes containing both. Place-object counts R aggregated over 61 training scenes give p(P|O) and p(O|P), built from 10 random-exploration episodes per scene.

Relation update: in a test episode, Bayesian-style count updates with rate 0.1 of the max count. If the target is not found in the expected place, that place-object link weakens and the next most likely place is explored.

Global policy: localize the current place by cosine similarity to cluster centroids; target place = argmax p(P|O_goal). Subgoal candidates for front, left and right come from the most important object (inverse entropy) in each direction. The chosen subgoal has the highest reachability product along a semantic shortest path (edge weight -log Γ), and unreachable candidates are pruned NRNS-style.

Local policy: FMM shortest path on a depth-derived local obstacle map using local pose; the action space is forward 0.4 m, turn 30°, stop. Stopping uses an object approach-and-check rule plus a place-based stop.
Localization probe: a GNN plus transformer decoder over the graph predicts the distance between a query and a target image node to test the value of semantic information.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 place/image/object encoders (trained), MaskRCNN detector (trained on MP3D 40 categories), FMM local planner, count-based SEA
setting.training_data: MP3D 61 train scenes: 5,000 random panoramic RGB images per scene (305,000) for encoders, ground truth objects and place labels; 610 exploration episodes to build SEA; non-interactive, no RL
setting.observation: 640x480 RGB-D plus 512x128 panoramic RGB; local pose sensor used only by the local policy; no global pose
setting.action_space: low-level: forward 0.4 m, turn left/right 30°, stop (500-step budget, success 1.0 m)
setting.privileged: none at test time (ground-truth place labels and objects are used for training only)

numbers.extra: no global pose; Table marks pose-noise robustness; no RL training
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Habitat ObjectNav results on MP3D: SEA (ours) 39.0 / 13.7 / 5.0

numbers_note: Pose-noise robustness and training cost are shown only in figures. Localization results (Acc@0.5m 40.4, Acc@1m 73.1) are a probe task, not navigation, so they are omitted from the numbers.
results: SEA reaches 39.0 SR, 13.7 SPL and 5.0 DTS on MP3D val, beating SemExp+SI (34.7 SR) by 12.4% relative, and PONI (31.8) too. SPL is below SemExp+SI's 15.1. It degrades much less under pose noise and has about three times lower training cost than PONI.
limitations: Relies on ground-truth object and place labels for training the encoders, and on a good detector; the atlas is built from only 10 episodes per scene, so some places are not covered.
Priors from training scenes can mismatch a test scene (e.g. chest of drawers in a living room), so success requires costly re-exploration; SPL is lower than SemExp+SI.
Evaluated only on MP3D in simulation, with no real-robot tests; still needs local pose and depth for the local policy.
